page.layout: One page of text, one column of verse-like lines with a centred line ("Et sequitur:") and a signature at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: publicè dudum editum (ut Illyricus habet) contra infulsas & noxias monachorum rixas: ut de conceptione D. Virginis, & similibus obscuris, ociosis ac inutilibus, & interim publicæ quieti perniciosis controversiis. Cuius sententia sic subscribit[?] nostræ ætate Baptista Mantuanus, in 12. Fastorum libro:
Pullulat hac radice grauis discordia rixæ.
Sunt etenim, qui conceptus contagia in iftos
Lapsa uclint, magnamq; putent traxisse parentes
Fomitis antiqui uitium, cui fecit Origo
Nominis. Sunt alij, quibus hæc absurda uidentur,
Sicq; duæ ueniunt ista in certamina secta,
Nonnunquam magno implentes subsellia risu:
Æquanimes autem uolunt ut fi uera fateri,
Vanus utrq; labor, pietas temeraria, præceps
Religio, leuitas uelata scientiæ amictu.
Nec natura potest illuc extendere uisum,
Nec Deus hoc docuit, nec re dependet ab ista
Nostra salus. Quæ nos igitur dementia torquet,
Vt studeamus in his consumere litibus annos?
Et sequitur:
Quid, seu munda fuit semper, seu forduit olim
Hæc ea, Mortales, non sunt quæ numina posc unt
Obsequia à nobis, studio dominatur in isto
Ambitio, & tumidis pugnans iactantia verbis.

page.notes: The scan is damaged in places and several words are only partly legible; the uncertain readings are marked [?]. The line "Quid, seu munda..." and the verse lines are copied as printed, with line breaks treated as paragraphs. The signature "Ai" at the lower right and the page number "399" are read from a faint impression and may be inexact. The printer's spelling (e.g. "posc unt", "subscribit") was copied as seen.
